corrections: Replaced the single generic TankInventory class with two separately inspectable top-level component classes, Tank1Inventory and Tank2Inventory, so each named physical unit appears as its own component file while preserving the same legacy-note balance form der(level)=(inflow-outflow)/area.

Fixed the root-cause topology issue behind the unused TK_102.outflowActual_m3s connector: the previous system routed Tank 2 inflow both from TK_101.outflowActual_m3s and from zeroFlow.y, which over-constrained TK_102.inflow_m3s and bypassed the downstream terminal path. The revised system keeps the actual topology SRC-101 -> XV-101 -> TK-101 -> XV-102 -> TK-102 -> XV-103 -> DRN-101 by using TK_102.outflowActual_m3s as the terminal discharge connection and removing the incorrect extra inflow connection.

The terminal sink DRN-101 is represented in this signal-flow bundle by the zeroFlow RealExpression acting only as a non-accumulating downstream terminus for Tank 2 actual discharge. This is an assumption required because the chosen signal-flow formulation uses scalar flow signals rather than acausal Fluid boundary components.

The model preserves the brief's adopted legacy-note balances and the Merge assumption to use ideal Boolean valve commands directly as flow switches, rather than introducing valve stroke dynamics or an unstated hydraulic pressure-drop law.

The physical cutoff law preserves nonnegative inventory and prevents filling above 1.0 m by limiting actual outflow when empty and suppressing net inflow when full inside each tank balance. This uses the stated measurement-valid range 0.0..1.0 m as the physical bound because the brief does not provide a separate approved saturation law beyond that range.

Command pulses are implemented with BooleanTable using paired toggle times per occurrence and width cmdWidth = 2*scanPeriod = 0.2 s so each scheduled START, STOP, and SHUT press is visible to the sampled PLC logic, matching the stated 0.1 s scan time.
